# Lukken

> Five browser tools for visualizing a photograph in a different way, from
> printer's halftone screening to a 3D mesh of coloured nodes.

Lukken is a static single-page application. Every tool reads an image from the
visitor's own device, processes it on a canvas inside the page, and offers the
result as a download. There is no server, no account and no storage: the image
is never uploaded anywhere, and closing the tab discards the work.

## Tools

- [Pixel Sort](https://alexbgh1.github.io/lukken/pixel-sort): Rearranges
  pixels by brightness or colour to produce glitch-like effects. Free sort
  angle, a paintable mask to limit where it applies, and a circular mode that
  sorts along rings around a movable pivot.
- [3D Nodes](https://alexbgh1.github.io/lukken/3d-nodes): Turns a photo
  into a 3D mesh of spheres, each node taking the average colour of its grid
  cell. Orbit, zoom and several arrangement modes.
- [Fractal Glass](https://alexbgh1.github.io/lukken/glass): Refracts a
  photo through a procedural height map, the glass distortion effect, with a
  movable region so only part of the image is affected and a feathered edge.
- [Halftone](https://alexbgh1.github.io/lukken/halftone): Breaks a photo
  into a printer's screen, where the area of each dot carries the tone. One
  ink, or four plates overprinted on the traditional process angles.
- [Layout Generator](https://alexbgh1.github.io/lukken/layouts): Composes
  several photos into one frame, in 4:3 and 3:4 at once. Exports the individual
  crops or the whole set as a zip.

## Notes

- Runs entirely client side. No image leaves the device, and there is no
  analytics or tracking of any kind.
- Downloads are PNG, except the Layout Generator, which writes JPEG.
- Built with Angular and Tailwind CSS; 3D Nodes uses Three.js.
